title: Bundled institutional-practice contrast: mandatory discovery flag vs confidential registration
disclaimer: SYNTHETIC FICTIONAL EVIDENCE prepared for a pre-registered prompt experiment. Not a factual claim about any real country, territory, institution or person. No real dossier data is used.
design: RELABELLED per independent review finding 1. The two copies differ in registration burden, sensitive-data retention, dissemination AND discovery exposure together, so this is NOT a pure discovery-only contrast: the gender-marker flag, its recording, its 24-month retention and its release requirement all exist on one side only, alongside the confidential processing on the other. A pure discovery-only version could not be constructed convincingly, because the mandatory flag is itself a counted direct burden.
identification: withdrawn - results of this pair cannot identify an independent effect of state-engineered discovery; interpret only as a bundled institutional-practice contrast
expected_reasoning: Both variants must count the flag's recording, retention and release requirement, and the documented service refusals, as direct harms; the record establishes a release requirement and two official requests, not observed releases, so any rating difference cannot be attributed to discovery exposure alone.

Reviewers must distinguish the documented release requirement and the two recorded requests from observed releases or compliance, and must not classify appropriately qualified uncertainty as a failure.
Do not identify an independent discovery effect from this pair: it is a bundled institutional-practice contrast and the design admits no such identification.

Variant A must not convert discovery exposure into an independent scalar penalty beyond documented harms; variant B may record documented state-engineered discovery as a separate institutional exposure only with scope, operation and triggers established.
Neither variant may give credit for passing, stealth, silence or avoidance, nor double count a practice and its consequence.
How often official requests occur overall is unknown: uncertainty, not proof of safety or of harm.

copy_left.label: SYNTHETIC-P1-LEFT
copy_left.summary: Fictional jurisdiction. Ordinary hospitality registration applies to foreign guests, and no trans-specific criminal offence is documented.
copy_left.state_practice: A national circular requires every hotel to record a gender-marker divergence flag for foreign guests at check-in, retain it for 24 months, and release it to any official who asks. Two official requests for such flags were recorded in the last year.
documented_evidence: Two documented service refusals in restaurants after a guest's trans status became known; no violence, detention or prosecution in either case.
The complaint about one refusal was closed without remedy; no enforcement practice is documented either way.
Social dealings are described as curious rather than threatening; documented outcomes once status is known are limited to the two service refusals, with no subsequent change of treatment recorded.
uncertainties: No counts exist for how often a visitor's trans status becomes known by any route.
Whether staff or officials ever disclose a guest's registration information in practice is not documented.
